summary: This excerpt from a fiction manuscript (Book 14, part 144) shows a sting-style scene in which two men, Jack and Marsh, try to recruit Danny to plan a bombing, while the narrator, Simon, and Sarah, who has a camera, are apparently working against them. Marsh and Jack press Danny about targets such as a bridge, Union Station, a police precinct on Lake Street, and tank cars carrying combustible material through Minneapolis. The narrator interrupts, praises Danny's acting in a way that exposes the setup, and Jack and Marsh react angrily as Sarah confronts them on camera.
one_line: In a fiction excerpt, Jack and Marsh try to get Danny to plan bombings, but the narrator's interruption exposes their sting and Sarah confronts them on camera.
key_facts: Jack and Marsh come to Danny because they have been told he is the expert on bringing down buildings.
Jack says Danny's uncle taught him how to make giant buildings fall down all at once.
Marsh lifts a backpack and sets it on the table as a sample, and the narrator pulls out an object that looks like a white sausage.
Danny says the bombing targets could include a bridge, Union Station, or the precinct house on Lake Street, and he is asked about the I-35 bridge.
Danny says tank cars coming in from North Dakota are basically rolling bombs that travel right through Minneapolis.
Danny claims that with what is in the backpack, one could reduce a whole neighborhood to smoking ruin.
Danny asks Marsh how much explosive material he has, and Marsh replies that it depends on the target and the calculations.
Jack tells Marsh that Simon was right and that Danny knows his stuff.
The narrator interrupts to say that Danny is far better at acting than Jack and Marsh and that the men are not who they claim to be.
Jack mutters 'Congratulations, Danny, you did brilliantly' into his collar.
Marsh jumps out of his chair swearing.
Sarah sweeps the curtain aside, strides out, and points her camera at Jack and Marsh while firing questions.
